Oti Region

Oti

Water shapes the journeys here, linking lakeside communities, working boats and green inland roads.

A boat crossing Lake Volta · Photo: Celestinesucess

Capital

Dambai

Go for

Lake Volta, fishing towns and forest

Good to know

The region reaches deep into the Lake Volta basin.

Festivals in
Oti.

Festivals and cultural events kept here, in calendar order. Many dates move from year to year, so each festival’s page has what we know about when.

  • Feb

    Fussikur

    Bowiri remembers its journey from Moree: a week of rites, a climb to the old settlement and a grand durbar.

    Between February and MarchBowiri Amanforo

  • Apr

    Hyirebo

    A week of peace that closes the Bowiri year: river bathing at dawn, white clay and a durbar.

    The first week of AprilBowiri Amanforo

  • Aug

    Gidifon

    The Adele new yam festival: offerings of mashed yam on the mountain, then yam fufu and dancing at home.

    August to SeptemberThe Adele towns around Tutukpene

  • Sep

    Gyogyi

    The Akyode yam festival: the stool blesses the new yam, chiefs swear to the chief priest, and the night is for dancing.

    Usually September (the season runs August to November)The Akyode towns around Keri and Nkwanta

  • Sep

    Krachi Yam Festival

    Krachi and its yam-growing neighbours give thanks for the harvest, with masquerades and yam pounded in the open.

    SeptemberKete Krachi

  • Oct

    Buem Lilu

    The Buem yam festival: three weeks of rites in the towns, then a grand durbar at Bodada.

    Usually the second week of October; the Buem Traditional Council sets the dateBodada and the Buem towns

  • Oct

    Frikooso Afahye

    Tapa remembers the battle at Frikooso hill, where its people and their allies turned back an Asante army.

    OctoberTapa Abotoase and the Tapa towns

  • Nov

    Ovazu

    The Akposo thanksgiving for the fonio harvest, to God and the seven principal Akposo gods.

    At the fonio harvest, October to DecemberThe Akposo towns, Biakoye District
